added_failures_note: the reviewed manifest carries no baseline_suite/after_suite keys, but names the equivalent pair in test_logs: gate-main.log at head 06c368dce (14 failed, 1101 passed, 1 skipped, 2 warnings, 1 error, EXIT=1), delta-head.log rerunning those 14 ids at head (14 failed, EXIT=1) and delta-base.log rerunning the same 14 ids with reckon/crew/queue_admission.py, reckon/crew/dispatch.py and reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py reverted to 43677d0d (14 failed, EXIT=1); no id fails in one arm and passes in the other, so the change adds 0 failures. findings.text: the upstream hold is written only inside the local-lane-held branches (is_local at :1652 and :1723), so a node whose section waits are unmet and whose lane has room launches immediately against sections that have not been built, and no arm covers that path because both new dispatch arms pin session_slots=0 at tests/test_a_queued_request_waits_on_its_dependencies.py:283 and :301; whether the free-lane case belongs to plan section 2's "a queued request" or to the node goal's "a dispatched node" is a reading the coordinator should settle.

queue_requests is the batch producer plan section 2's "queue a whole width in one call" needs and no production module calls it — grep at the reviewed head finds it only in the new test module — so that half stays inert until section 5's crew queue verbs land, and plan section 2's other two wait kinds (a gate, another queued request named by id) are implemented nowhere.
advance_waiting_requests accepts a now argument its body never reads and admit_once passes now=moment at :1594, so the parameter advertises a time-dependence the pass does not have.

the tests line still carries an unsubstituted placeholder for the gate command, and gate-main.log's own command header repeats the placeholder with the targets on a separate line, so promotion's gate receipt cannot be re-run from either field.

the base arm's node-test arm fails four of five on AttributeError (no attribute queue_requests) rather than on the ordering the done_when claims, and the added ordering probe prints launched: 0 in both trees, so it observes the stored phases rather than a base launch.
